summary:
The Secure America Act (Public Law 119-98), enacted June 10, 2026, provides for reconciliation pursuant to title II of S. Con. Res. 33 by appropriating funds to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for fiscal year 2026, to remain available until September 30, 2029. 

Title I appropriates funds for functions other than immigration and customs enforcement. Section 101 appropriates $9,550,000,000 to the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) for Border Patrol agents and support personnel, with a restriction prohibiting funds for processing coordinators after October 31, 2028. Section 102 appropriates $7,450,000,000 to the Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents and operations, of which $108,500,000 is directed to child exploitation investigators and forensic analysts at the Victim Identification Laboratory and HSI offices. Section 103 appropriates $3,450,000,000 to CBP for nonintrusive inspection equipment, Air and Marine operations, border surveillance technology, and the biometric entry and exit system under 8 U.S.C. 1365b. It restricts funds for surveillance towers along the southwest and northern borders lacking tested autonomous capabilities, defining "autonomous" as systems applying artificial intelligence or similar algorithms to operate without continuous human command or control. Section 104 appropriates $2,500,000,000 to the Secretary of Homeland Security for Title I purposes.

Title II appropriates funds for immigration enforcement. Section 201 appropriates $13,020,000,000 to CBP for agents and support staff to carry out immigration enforcement activities. Section 202 appropriates $31,075,000,000 to ICE for personnel, transportation, IT, facility and fleet maintenance, 287(g) agreements under 8 U.S.C. 1357(g), and Office of the Principal Legal Advisor attorneys. It directs not less than $350,000,000 for detainer management and arrests of "covered unlawful aliens" in jurisdictions that are not "qualified cooperating jurisdictions," explicitly excluding Indian tribal governments from this designation. It defines "qualified cooperating jurisdiction" as a state or political subdivision with an active 287(g) agreement or certified compliance with 8 U.S.C. 1373 and 8 U.S.C. 1644. Funds under this provision may not be used to release, parole, or facilitate the release of encountered covered unlawful aliens. "Covered unlawful alien" is defined by reference to 8 U.S.C. 1226(c)(1), 1182(a)(2), 1227(a)(2), detainer requests under 8 U.S.C. 1226, 1231(a), or 1357, or charges or convictions under 8 U.S.C. 1325 or 1326. Section 203 appropriates $2,500,000,000 to the Secretary for Title II purposes or paragraphs (3) or (7) of section 100051 of Public Law 119-21. All appropriations are out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated.
